Effect attestation redesign — Q&A record
Effect attestation redesign — Q&A record > Q1 — "The pin updates are very manual. How do we automate them and avoid misuse? I'm thinking a DSL in commit messages so hooks update pins automatically."

Effect attestation redesign — Q&A record > Q2 — "Is the TRUE cause the existence of the pin in the content? In caveman.md the commit hash exists in both frontmatter and body. The repo value in the body should live in the source page's frontmatter; branch should use the source's tracking reference; commit/checksum should be references if needed at all — they are repeated information. The problem is DRY. The bigger issue: effects don't use 'source', and no lint enforces it. Would fixing this make the whole pin process mechanical?"
Effect attestation redesign — Q&A record > Q3 — "Before deciding what to fix, let's dig into the underground truth. What is effect? Show me your understanding."

Effect attestation redesign — Q&A record > Q4 — "What should the effect be? Rethink the primitives: an effect is a md file, both executable and readable. It can be 'applied'; once applied it saves the pointed record of applying — this is the proof of effect (the commit). The commit+location answer the question of where, the checksum is the proof. Combining them, they became attestation. So what we need is the attestation of effect. Multiple effects combine into one effect, sharing the same interface — currently ^check and ^install, which don't match the semantics we found. We should have skills/SKILLS.md as the entrypoint of one effect kind. Root EFFECTS.md defines the interface for the effects domain and obeys the LLM-WIKI interface: each root-level folder should contain a ^check block — a one-line rule."

Effect attestation redesign — Q&A record > Q5 — "The one-line rule is a blurb, right? Each root folder should have a blurb; the LLM-WIKI root contract needs one blurb per folder and does not care what's inside — not its care scope. Now the members inside effects — this reminds me of what Nix designed. A source page records where it's from; drift = pin vs tracking branch. An effect page does attestation: an effect is a claim (for skills: symlink correctness); a failed attestation means re-apply/realise. A rootless effect is void and can be abused — but requiring roots elsewhere creates garbage, so an effect can come from itself for ad-hoc. Composability is NOT one apply triggering many applies — it's the attestation chain, the deeper internal relationships. draws-from is weak — 'might be coming from' — but those ARE the attestation chain: any item breaks, the effect should be re-evaluated. Ideally: a new domain page that affects a skill gets added to the chain, with an optional claim string (optional because the dependency-add changes the attestation doc anyway). To be practical at scale, a chain item can reference a wikilink's section content — if the section content doesn't change, it's valid; this requires resolving wikilinks inside the section. When any dependent changes, an alignment process runs: base defined in effects/EFFECTS, overridden in skills/SKILLS.md and children — (1) mechanical, hard cheap checks; (2) instructional, structured checklist output, executed by one agent, reviewed by another, orchestrated with dynamic workflow. Build the meridian of the wiki — 经络, not our tool."

Effect attestation redesign — Q&A record > Q6 — "The md tool should resolve wikilinks: embeds always resolve, references by specified depth, structured data with content plus link count per resolution; depth 1 is most useful; full resolution requires cache. Tier-2 alignment can be cached — agents write verdicts to the ucc session folder, committed at home-wiki-sessions. On cycles: acyclic in each commit, loop by design — effect A ships, the source records it, domain D updates, effects A B C are affected; A must NOT be excluded from re-eval (its good change may combine badly with B and C); agents revert or iterate A B C together; endless loops are avoided by a budget on re-alignment, readable from the realise commit messages — baked into the design, not our worry now. And the deeper view: ancient Chinese medicine was built on experience and experiments — the Nix way is the Western approach; they don't compete, they complete each other. Tags look like 穴位. 望 = check, cheap, from a distance; 闻 = ??; 问 = git history, the past; 切 = ??. Does this ring a bell for the two challenges?"

Effect attestation redesign — Q&A record > Q7 — "Let's not design the 闻-mining, but observe. Humans can feel what smells good or bad; we can't. If it is too obvious, it's 'look'. By admitting it honestly, we can faithfully find out what it means to us by creating the system. After everything unfolds, and after I have the ability to smell the system's odor, then we continue the journey of exploration."
